What could we move?”

passage: Sunday night. I'm too tired to think properly, so this will be short. Tuition at 4, unit test tomorrow, Mausi's family here for lunch, and Payal and I said we'd go to the shop for chart paper. I was okay until dinner. Then Payal asked if I could pass the salt and I said “Can't you see I'm busy?” loudly enough that everyone looked up. Payal's face went small. Ma didn't say anything, just kept eating. I feel awful. The strange thing is I wasn't angry at Payal at all. I think I'm just full, like a glass that's been overflowing all day. I'll say sorry in the morning. — Himani

subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
passage: Anand, fifteen, had unit tests all week, coaching till eight every evening, and his cousin's wedding on Saturday, where the family expected him to help. His friends had also planned a cricket match. On Thursday night, while he was trying to memorise chemical formulas, his younger brother Suraj came in to ask about a school project. "Can't you see I'm busy?" Anand snapped. Suraj's face crumpled and he walked out. Anand stared at the formulas and felt awful. It wasn't about Suraj. He went next door. "Sorry. I'm just stretched too thin this week. Can we do your project on Sunday?" Suraj nodded, and Anand crossed the cricket match off his list.

qa.q: What event was the family expecting Anand to help with?
qa.a: His cousin's wedding on Saturday.

qa.q: What was Anand feeling after he snapped at Suraj?
qa.a: He felt awful and guilty, realising his irritation came from being overloaded, not from Suraj.

qa.q: What did Anand do to repair things, and what else helped?
qa.a: He apologised, explained he was stretched thin, offered Sunday for the project and crossed the cricket match off his list.

qa.q: What is it like for Suraj when Anand snaps?
qa.a: Suraj feels hurt, his face crumpling, since he just wanted help and did not know how much his brother was carrying.

grounding: Shows a teenager pulled between tests, coaching, a family wedding and friends, whose overload shows as snapping at his brother.

subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
passage: In their Delhi flat, Hrithik, sixteen, had a coaching test on Sunday, a school practical on Monday, and his grandparents visiting for the week. His friends wanted him at a birthday on Saturday. He hadn't said anything to anyone about feeling stretched. At dinner, his sister Hafsa asked him to pass the dal. "Get it yourself," he said sharply. The table went quiet. Hafsa's eyes widened. Later, their mother found him on the balcony. "What's going on?" He shrugged, then blurted it out: the tests, the practical, the birthday, everyone needing him. She listened. "Let's see what can move." He skipped the birthday, and apologised to Hafsa before bed.

qa.q: What did Hafsa ask Hrithik to pass?
qa.a: She asked him to pass the dal.

qa.q: Why did Hrithik snap at Hafsa?
qa.a: He felt overwhelmed and pulled apart by tests, the practical, visiting grandparents and a birthday, and the pressure came out as irritability.

qa.q: How did their mother help, and why did it work?
qa.a: She asked what was going on and listened, then helped him see what could move, so he could drop the birthday.

qa.q: How might Hafsa have felt at dinner?
qa.a: Hafsa was probably shocked and hurt, her eyes widening, since passing the dal was a simple request.

grounding: Illustrates a teenager juggling tests, family and friends whose overload first shows as snapping at his sister.

passage:
Akash: "Rashmi didi, can you help me with my maths?"
Rashmi: "Not now!"
Akash: "You didn't even look at it."
Rashmi: "I have tuition in twenty minutes, physics test tomorrow, and Mausi's coming tonight and Ma wants me to make the tea."
Akash: "I just asked about one sum."
Rashmi: (sighs) "Sorry. I'm not angry at you."
Akash: "You've been angry all week."
Rashmi: "I know. Everything wants me at the same time."
Akash: "Why don't you tell Ma?"
Rashmi: "She'll say everyone has exams."
Akash: "Tell her anyway. I can make the tea."
Rashmi: (small smile) "You can't make tea."
Akash: "I'll learn. Show me the sum after tuition?"
Rashmi: "Deal."

qa.a: Rashmi had tuition in twenty minutes.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling when she snapped at Akash?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and pulled apart by tuition, a test, a visitor and chores, and the stress came out as irritation.

qa.q: What small step could help Rashmi this week?
qa.a: Telling Ma honestly how much is on her plate, and letting Akash take over the tea, would lighten the load.

qa.q: What is it like for Akash to be snapped at all week?
qa.a: Akash feels confused and a bit hurt, but also notices Rashmi's mood and offers to help.

subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
passage: Looking back, I can see it clearly, but at the time I just thought everyone was being annoying. That was the week of my pre-board maths paper. Coaching ran from five to eight. My cousin's nikah was on Saturday, and Ammi needed me to fetch chairs from the tent house. Yash kept messaging about his birthday football match. Nobody asked me how I was, and I didn't say. Instead, when my little brother asked me to help with his kite, I shouted so loudly that he cried. I slammed the door on Ammi over a cup of tea. On Thursday Yash said, "Irfan, you've been biting everyone's head off." That was the first time I thought: oh. I'm not angry at them. I'm stretched too thin.

qa.q: When did Irfan's coaching run that week?
qa.a: Coaching ran from five to eight.

qa.q: What was Irfan really feeling underneath the shouting?
qa.a: Irfan was overwhelmed and pulled apart by the paper, coaching, the nikah and Yash's match; the irritation was the overload showing, not real anger at the family.

qa.q: What small step could have helped Irfan earlier in that week?
qa.a: Irfan could have told Ammi and Yash how packed the week was and asked for one thing to move, such as someone else fetching the chairs.

qa.q: What was it like for Irfan's little brother when he asked about the kite?
qa.a: He asked for a small, happy thing and got shouted at, so he was hurt and confused and cried, not knowing what he had done.
